correctness.rationale: The finite-trace weak-next formula is satisfied precisely by nondecreasing 0^a1^(n-a) words. A violating AXp is a minimal fixed earlier-1/later-0 inverted pair; its CXps are minimal cut-difference sets D_c at rises 01 and eligible endpoints. Thus counts are inversion_10(w) and descent_10(w)+1, the binomial transition-count spectrum is binom(n+1,2d+1), and satisfying families follow from mandatory singleton changes plus the boundary pair. Checked n=1 exceptional empty AXp and n=2 boundary. Independent direct completion/subset enumerator reproduced both minimal families for all 254 binary traces of lengths 1..7; general n relies on cut-structure proof, not enumeration.
residual_risks: Finite cross-checks are corroboration, not universal proof.
